public_rationale: RD Michigan provides a contractual exception. KBRA and Fitch describe fixed-date rent commencement and protections against late delivery; Fitch also describes customer carrying-cost obligations during qualifying power delays. Customer support therefore does not universally depend on completed usable delivery. Many other deals do expose lenders to completion-dependent rent, but that does not sustain “every single.” This assessment concerns contractual obligations, not evidence that delay payments were already collected.
limitations: Rating-agency descriptions substitute for the executed leases.
The outcome depends on the contractual reading of payment dependence.
The evidence does not show actual pre-completion collections or remove all construction risk.

evidence.explanation: Fitch independently describes the AI-suitable facility's fixed-date rent and says the tenant must cover carrying costs after qualifying power delays if the landlord elects. This is evidence of contractual customer support despite delayed usable delivery, not proof that such payments had already been collected.
Supports Zitron's underlying concern for many financings. It does not establish an exceptionless rule and falls outside the selected observation quarter.
